en: The Questions of Milinda,
Great Chapter 5: The Question on Going Forth into the Homeless Life (Pabbajjapañha)
Then the Venerable Nāgasena approached the residence of King Milinda; having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat.

Then King Milinda, with his own hands, satisfied and served the Venerable Nāgasena and his assembly with choice hard and soft foods, and after providing each monk with a pair of garments, he [proceeded].
Having clothed the Venerable Nāgasena with the three robes, he said this to the Venerable Nāgasena:
“Venerable Nāgasena, sit here together with ten bhikkhus; let the rest depart.
Then King Milinda, having seen that the Venerable Nāgasena had finished eating and had put away his bowl and hands, [approached] another...
Taking a low seat, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King Milinda said this to the Venerable Nāgasena:
"Venerable Nāgasena, about what shall our conversation and discussion take place?"
“We, Great King, have need of the goal; let there be a discussion concerning the goal.
The king said, “Venerable Nāgasena, for what purpose is your going forth, and what is your ultimate goal?”
The Elder said:
“How, Great King, might this suffering cease, and how might further suffering not arise?
It is for this purpose, Great King, that we have gone forth; but our ultimate goal, Great King, is final Nibbāna through non-clinging.”
“But, venerable Nāgasena, do all go forth for this purpose?
“Certainly not, great king. Some go forth for this purpose; some go forth driven by a king;
some go forth driven by thieves; some go forth oppressed by debt; some go forth for the sake of a livelihood.”
“But those who go forth rightly, they go forth for this purpose.
“But you, venerable sir, have you gone forth for this purpose?
“I, great king, went forth while still young; I did not know that I was going forth for the sake of this name.”
"Moreover, this thought occurred to me: 'These recluses, sons of the Sakyan, are wise;
they will train me. Thus, having been trained by them, I now know and see: 'For this purpose is renunciation.
"Excellent, Bhante Nāgasena!"
The fifth question on going forth.
